title: S2 default /map view is read-only — map-click never adds an intersection
body:
## Summary

On S2 (`/map`), the default view is the read-only flow map, so **clicking the map never opens the add-intersection modal**. Map-click only reaches `openAdd` when `viewMode === 'edit'`, but `/map` defaults to `'pre'`/`'post'` and there's no UI affordance that switches to `'edit'` for adding. Today the only way to add an intersection by map-click is to manually load `/map?view=edit`.

## Where

`frontend/src/sessions/S2_MapIntersection.jsx` — `handleMapClick`:

```js
const handleMapClick = (latlng) => {
  if (viewMode === 'pre' || viewMode === 'post') {   // read-only: returns early
    if (flowPopup) setFlowPopup(null)
    return
  }
  if (mapMode === 'intersections') { openAdd(latlng); return }  // only reachable in 'edit'
  ...
}
```

- `initialViewMode()` returns `lastRun ? 'post' : 'pre'` — never `'edit'` without a `?view=edit` query param.
- The "Modify links" toggle (`switchMode('links')`) does set `viewMode='edit'`, but it also sets `mapMode='links'`, so clicks route to link-drawing, not `openAdd`. Leaving link mode reverts `viewMode` to `'pre'`/`'post'`.

Net: there is no obvious in-app path to add an intersection (including the **first** one) via map-click.

## Impact

This is very likely the real mechanism behind the "Add intersection silently fails" symptom from the state-corruption bug (#fixed in 2c9ec45): the corrupted "Willow" project had `analysis.lastRun` populated → `/map` defaulted to read-only `'post'` → clicks did nothing. The self-heal fix clears `lastRun`, but the default view is *still* read-only (`'pre'`), so map-click add remains gated even after recovery.

**Pre-existing** — not introduced by 2c9ec45. Surfaced during browser verification of that fix.

## Evidence (verified in Chrome against the running app)

- Clean project, default `/map`: map-click → add modal count **0**.
- Healed Willow project, default `/map`: map-click → add modal count **0**.
- Same click on `/map?view=edit`: modal opens, intersection added successfully.

## Suggested fixes (pick one)

1. Default `viewMode` to `'edit'` when the project has **0 intersections** (so the first add always works), falling back to `lastRun ? 'post' : 'pre'` once intersections exist.
2. Add an explicit **"Add intersection"** affordance (button / mode toggle) to the S2 flow toolbar that enters an editable, clickable state — independent of the link-drawing mode.
3. Add an "Edit" tab alongside Pre-balance / Post-balance in the flow toolbar.

Option 1 is the smallest change and directly unblocks the first-intersection case.

title: DemandIQ Forecasting v1 — Method 1 (NCHRP 765, SANDAG): engine · API · frontend · Corridor/Scenario VMT · multi-county groundwork
body:
## DemandIQ Forecasting v1 — Method 1 (NCHRP 765, SANDAG)

Model-based corridor forecasting end to end: a tested Python pipeline under
`backend/forecasting/`, the HTTP API that exposes it, the F1–F4 frontend that
drives it, Corridor + Scenario VMT, and the first two phases of region
generalization. SANDAG region only. **157 tests passing.**

### Pipeline
```
SANDAG hwyLoad.shp ─ingest─→ filtered NetworkLayer(s) ─match─→ leg→link bindings
                                            ─refine─→ future approach/exit totals (NCHRP 255)
                                            ─Pass 1─→ per-intersection future TMC matrix (IPF)
                                            ─Pass 2─→ corridor-conserved, rounded future TMCs
                                            ─VMT────→ corridor veh-mi (existing/future/Δ, + scenario)
```

### Engine — 7 modules (one commit each)
| Module | What |
|---|---|
| contract | `NetworkLink`/`NetworkLayer` — AB/BA convention encoded once; now also carries canonical `length_mi` + `daily_total` |
| SANDAG adapter | shapefile → canonical layer; geo deps lazy; filter-first; populates the canonical fields |
| ingest | per-year orchestration + base↔horizon overlap/ID-stability check; **region adapter registry** |
| matcher | node-snap + link-centric leg binding; flags for review |
| refinement | NCHRP 255, **ratio-operative** (see below) |
| Pass 1 | per-intersection IPF, seeded by base turn pattern |
| Pass 2 | corridor link conservation via the existing S6 `balance_nchrp` |

### API (under `/forecast`)
- **`POST /forecast/ingest-match`** — the **only geo-dependent route**. Ingests the
  network(s) + matches the base layer → `{layers, matches}` for the review UI.
  Returns **503** (not 500) if geo deps are absent; rejects shapefile paths outside
  `data/sandag/`.
- **`POST /forecast/run`** — pure Python. refine → Pass 1 → Pass 2 per period; folds in
  Corridor VMT (and a Scenario block when a reduction factor is supplied). Requires both
  `base` and `horizon` layers.

### Frontend (F1–F4 + handoff)
- **F1 — Horizon & Network setup:** tag base/horizon model years + SANDAG network file(s).
- **F2 — Network Match review:** pull the filtered network, two-pane map + per-leg review
  (matched/ambiguous/unmatched/absent) with candidate-pick / manual-entry / skip; the
  differentiator screen.
- **F3 — Run Forecast:** link-resolution + refinement-method settings (Ratio default; K
  unlocks Difference/Combined), run diagnostics per period.
- **F4 — Future Results:** future-vs-existing TMC table, comparison diagrams (existing vs
  future), methodology citation chip with click-to-expand per-leg provenance.
- **S8 "Continue to Forecasting →"** handoff CTA from the existing-conditions flow; Signal
  palette + charcoal theme (amber forecasting chrome, constant across light/dark).

### Corridor VMT
- **Deterministic engine** riding behind Pass 2: VMT = Σ(volume × length) over the
  **traced** model-link chain (Dijkstra node→node, lengths summed — no incident
  undercount), rolled up link → corridor → network, for existing / future / Δ.
- **Basis is pinned + labeled.** Peak-hour is always clean. Daily is count-anchored from
  the model's own per-corridor daily/period ratio when present (**data-derived, no
  asterisk**); falls back to an engineer expansion factor (**asterisk + note**); omitted
  otherwise (peak-hour still clean). Held/untraceable segments are hold-flat-and-flag.
- **Surfaced** in the `/run` response, an F4 panel (green existing / amber future, unit +
  basis on its face) with a provenance chip, and a dedicated **"Corridor VMT" Excel sheet**
  (per-period summary + per-link breakdown + network rollup; caveats travel with the
  numbers — same fields the F4 chip reads, so workbook and UI can't disagree).
- **Verified end-to-end on a real export render**, not just unit tests.

### Scenario VMT
- Engineer-supplied **demand-reduction factor** (e.g. a TDM / bike-lane assumption). Scales
  the forecast volumes by `(1 − f)` and re-runs the **same** VMT engine — baseline vs.
  scenario vs. Δ (and %), peak-hour basis, daily carried through with the same asterisk
  discipline.
- **Trust line:** the tool **applies** the factor the engineer supplies — it never
  generates, suggests, or carries a built-in library of reduction factors. The factor and a
  "scenario" label travel onto both the F4 panel and the export, so a mitigated number can
  never be read as the unmitigated forecast.
- Full path: engine (`scenario_factor`) → API (`scenario_reduction_factor` on `/run`) →
  export (labeled Scenario block) → F4 (percent input with a neutral helper, no preset value).

### Multi-county groundwork (Phases 1–2 of region generalization)
- **Phase 1 — name the seam:** `ingest.py` dispatches through a **region adapter registry**
  instead of a hardcoded `if region != "SANDAG"`; an unregistered region fails loud with the
  available adapters listed. Adding a region = register an adapter, not edit a conditional.
- **Phase 2 — close the canonical-field leaks (a latent-defect fix):** the VMT engine no
  longer reads SANDAG column strings out of `source_attributes` (`ab_*_flow`, `total_flow`,
  `len_mile`). `NetworkLink` gained typed `length_mi` + `daily_total`, populated by the
  adapter; the engine reads the contract. Behavior-preserving — identical numbers out.
- **Spec at `Docs/forecasting-multicounty.md`.** Scope is *one region per project*,
  *SANDAG-shaped models*, *speculative* (no second consumer yet). **Phases 3–5 are
  deliberately deferred** (declarative region schema + the suggest-confirm schema-mapping
  agent + web-dictionary lookup; period-scheme/flow-basis generalization; region-aware
  UI/API copy). **Promotion trigger documented:** a concrete second MPO model arriving
  promotes Phases 3 + 5 into active work, validated against the real schema rather than an
  imagined one.

### Included from main — QC-08 corridor-order fix (#4)
This branch has merged `main`, which carries the QC-08 fix from **#4** (already
reviewed and merged). So the `backend/balancer.py` + `backend/test_balancer_nchrp.py`
changes in this diff are **that fix, not new forecasting work**: `run_qc`'s QC-08
post-balance residual check now pairs adjacent intersections in corridor (given-list)
order — the same order `balance_corridor` uses — instead of `sorted(intersections,
key=num)`, which diverged from the corridor (and from `2_Intersections`) whenever IDs
weren't entered in ascending order. Ships with a regression test.

### Key engineering decisions
- **Reuse over rebuild.** Pass 1 reuses `balancer.furness_intersection`; Pass 2 reuses
  `balancer.balance_nchrp` — the same engines S6 runs on observed counts, now on the
  forecast. Scenario VMT re-runs the *same* `corridor_vmt`, one multiplier, no fork. F4's
  scenario re-run reuses F3's `/run` payload builder (`lib/forecastRun.js`), not a copy.
- **Geo-dep boundary = the ingest line, nowhere else.** Only the adapter touches
  geopandas/shapely/pyproj, lazily imported. `app.py` imports stay geo-free — the app starts
  under the lean interpreter with both routes registered; only the ingest *call* needs
  geopandas and degrades to **503**.
- **Ratio-operative refinement (verified data fact).** SANDAG `*_flow` fields are **period**
  volumes (`total_flow == Σ of the 10 period flows`, exactly; no peak-hour field) while
  DemandIQ counts are **peak-hour**. Ratio (time-base-invariant) is operative;
  Difference/Combined are gated on an engineer peak-hour factor K — never silently wrong.
- **Caveat travels with the number.** Daily asterisks, held-segment flags, and the scenario
  label are read from the same object fields the UI renders, so the Excel export and the F4
  chip can never disagree.

### Tests
- **157 tests pass** (includes the QC-08 ordering regression test merged from #4).
  Synthetic fixtures throughout; real-file integration gated on
  `data/sandag/hwyLoad.shp` (skipped on CI, run locally). API tests run the router on a bare
  `FastAPI()` + TestClient (no `app.py`/auth coupling). Frontend: eslint clean + production
  `vite build` passes.
- Run: `cd backend && .venv-forecasting/bin/python -m pytest` (combined venv =
  `requirements.txt` + `requirements-forecasting.txt`).

### Known limitations (please read before reviewing)
1. **No real base→2030 forecast has run.** Every forecast/VMT number to date is **synthetic
   or identity-growth** (base == horizon) — the real 2030 SANDAG network isn't on disk. The
   pipeline is proven end-to-end (including a real VMT export render); a real *client*
   forecast is gated on that file arriving.
2. **The forecasting-enabled app must run under the combined venv** (geo deps). The lean
   production image intentionally **503s** on `/forecast/ingest-match`; the pure `/forecast/run`
   path and the rest of the app are unaffected.

title: fix(QC-08): corridor adjacency from row order, not sorted intersection IDs
body:
## QC-08 (QC sheet) — corridor adjacency from row order, not sorted intersection IDs

### Problem
On the QC sheet, the intersection **numbering** and the inter-intersection **links** diverged from `2_Intersections`.

### Root cause
`run_qc` → QC-08 (post-balance residual) built its links from **`sorted(bal.keys())`** — ascending intersection *number* — then paired consecutive sorted entries. Every other sheet derives order from the **row-ordered `intersections` list** (row order = corridor order; `2_Intersections` and `balance_config`/`balance_corridor` all use it). QC-08 was the lone exception, so it only agreed with `2_Intersections` when the engineer happened to enter IDs in ascending corridor order.

### Fix
**A — row-order adjacency.** Pair consecutive intersections in row order, the same pairing `balance_config`/`balance_corridor` use, so the QC sheet matches `2_Intersections` by construction. Because row 6 = corridor origin, `up→dn` is genuinely upstream→downstream, which also corrects the EB/WB direction labels. Intersections missing from the balance result are skipped rather than paired non-adjacently across a gap (an improvement over the old sorted-keys behavior).

**B — direction-aware through-movement.** QC-08 hardcoded `EBT`/`WBT`, so **NB/SB corridors got no meaningful residual check**. It now selects the through-movement pair by `corridor_dir` (`EBT`/`WBT` for EB/WB, `NBT`/`SBT` for NB/SB). `corridor_dir` is threaded in from the existing `cfg` at the one call site.

Scope: `run_qc` + its single call site only. **Diagram styling (`ecr_v26`) untouched.**

### Verification
- `python3 -m py_compile 3_demand_analysis.py` — clean.
- Behavior: with IDs entered in ascending corridor order the output is unchanged; the fix only changes (corrects) cases where numbering wasn't monotonic with rows, and adds NB/SB coverage.

### Note on the base branch
`3_demand_analysis.py` was removed from mainline in `0d5d78f` ("remove legacy monolith"). To keep the diff to the fix alone and **avoid reintroducing the monolith to mainline**, this PR is based on `legacy/3demand-baseline` (the pristine pre-removal state at `0d5d78f^`), not `main`. `forecasting-v1-engine` is untouched.

title: fix(balancer): QC-08 pairs intersections in corridor order, not sorted by number
body:
## QC-08 pairs intersections in corridor order, not sorted by number

### Problem
`balancer.run_qc` → **QC-08** (post-balance residual gap) built its inter-intersection links by **sorting the intersections by number** (`sorted(intersections, key=lambda x: x['num'])`) and pairing consecutive entries. So its `Int X→Y` links diverged from the actual corridor whenever the engineer's IDs weren't entered in ascending corridor order — the same divergence reported between the QC sheet and `2_Intersections` in the legacy export (PR #3), now fixed in the live web-app path.

### Root cause
Every other consumer — `balance_corridor` in particular (`for i in range(len(intersections)-1): up=intersections[i]; dn=intersections[i+1]`) — pairs from the **given `intersections` order**, which *is* the corridor order. QC-08 was the lone consumer that re-sorted, so it only agreed with the corridor when numbering happened to ascend with it.

### Fix
QC-08 now iterates `intersections` in the **given (corridor) order**, identical to `balance_corridor` — so the links match the corridor by construction. Because the given order is corridor order, `up→dn` is genuinely upstream→downstream, and the direction labels are correct.

Direction-awareness (`EBT`/`WBT` for EB/WB, `NBT`/`SBT` for NB/SB) was **already** present in this path, so no other change was needed — the fix is the QC-08 body only; `app.py` already passes `corridor_dir`.

### Test
Adds `test_qc08_pairs_in_corridor_order_not_sorted_by_number`: with non-monotonic numbering (corridor order 3 → 1 → 2), QC-08 must flag the corridor-adjacent link **3→1** and must **not** emit the numeric-adjacent **2→3**. Fails on the old sorted-by-number code; passes on the fix. `backend/test_balancer_nchrp.py`: **23 passed**.

### Relationship to PR #3
PR #3 fixed the same defect in the removed legacy monolith (`3_demand_analysis.py`) on a dedicated branch. This PR ports the fix to the live app's QC path (`balancer.py`) and targets `main`, where the bug ships. `forecasting-v1-engine` is unaffected (it will pick this up when it next merges `main`).

title: fix(frontend): S7 results map draws corridor from explicit links, not array order
body:
## S7 results map: corridor from the explicit links graph, not array order

### Problem
The S7 results map disagreed with the S2 map on corridor topology — e.g. link **4→2** showed as **4→2** on S2 but **4→3** on S7 (its numeric neighbour). Classic signature of one surface deriving adjacency by number/position while the other uses the real corridor edges.

### Root cause
`ResultsMap` connected intersections with `L.polyline(intersections.map(...))` — **array (≈ numeric) order** — and took no `links` prop, ignoring the explicit `links` graph that the S2 map (`MapView.LinkLayer`) renders by `fromId/toId`. Same class as the QC‑08 fix, different surface.

### Fix (single source of truth)
- New `frontend/src/lib/corridorSegments.js` — `buildCorridorSegments(intersections, links)`, the one id‑based adjacency derivation (skips orphan links).
- `ResultsMap.jsx` accepts `links` and draws segments via the helper.
- `S7_Results.jsx` passes `snap.links` — the same store source S2 reads.

S7 now matches S2 by construction; no eye‑alignment, no hardcoded pair.

### Test
`node --test frontend/src/lib/corridorSegments.test.mjs` (Node built‑in runner, no new dep): non‑monotonic numbering (link 4→2 with num‑3 numerically between) asserts the segment is **4→2, not 4→3**; plus an orphan‑link skip case. eslint clean; `vite build` passes.

### Follow‑ups (not in this PR)
- `MapView.LinkLayer` could adopt `buildCorridorSegments` for full DRY (it already reads `links`, so not a second *adjacency* source).
- Backend `balance_corridor`/`run_qc` derive the corridor from **intersections list order**, a different model than the frontend's explicit `links` graph — worth its own diagnosis.

Proves the NCHRP-765 pipeline on **real, differential** growth and makes a real 2030 forecast a one-file swap — without waiting on the (not-yet-available) real 2030 SANDAG network. Everything to date had been synthetic/identity-growth.

### What's here
- **`backend/forecasting/synth_horizon.py`** — derives an explicitly-synthetic horizon network from the real base by scaling each link's flows by a per-functional-class factor (Freeway/Ramp 1.35 · Prime/Major Arterial 1.20 · Collector 1.10 · Local 1.05 · Connector 1.00 · Other 1.10). Pure `synthesize_horizon_gdf` + lazy-geo `synthesize_horizon_shp` (writes `data/sandag/hwyLoad_2030_synthetic.shp`, `--force` guard) + CLI. ## Math-soundness fuzz bot + CI-gap fix

A Hypothesis property-based fuzz bot over the **pure-numeric** forecasting/balancing pipeline (no geopandas, runs in lean CI), plus the CI wiring to run it. Design + plan: `Docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-05-math-soundness-fuzz-bot-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-05-math-soundness-fuzz-bot.md`.

### What it adds
- **Generators** (`backend/tests/forecasting/fuzz/generators.py`) — contract-valid corridors, single-intersection spines, consistent IPF inputs, and VMT cases, reusing the existing test idioms so generated inputs are always valid.
- **Properties** asserting 9 of the spec's 10 in-scope invariants against real production code (no mocks):
  - #1 link conservation, #2 non-negativity, #3 round-to-5, #4 IPF convergence, #6 corridor-order (`test_fuzz_balancer.py`)
  - #7 identity-growth conservation, #8 VMT scenario linearity, #10 daily all-or-none, #5 U-turn passthrough (`test_fuzz_pipeline.py`)
  - Invariant #9 (`total_flow` identity) is intentionally deferred to the geo/adapter layer (needs shapefiles) per spec §6.
- **`ci`/`nightly` Hypothesis profiles** (`conftest.py`): deterministic 150-example PR gate vs randomized 5000-example deep run.
- **CI gate** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): runs `pytest tests/forecasting/` on every PR — which also **fixes a pre-existing gap**: `run_tests.sh` never ran the forecasting pytest suite, so it had *no* CI coverage until now.
- **Nightly deep-run bot** (`.github/workflows/fuzz-nightly.yml`): scheduled 5000-example run; fails loudly in the Actions tab, **no auto-issues**.
- **Geo skip-gating** (`conftest.py`): synthetic-shapefile adapter/ingest/synth-horizon tests now skip cleanly when the geo stack is absent (mirrors the existing `REAL_SHP` skipif), so the lean CI gate is green-or-skip with zero errors.

### Notable findings (the bot earning its keep)
Three properties were corrected from the plan because they over-claimed precision the production math never promised — in each case the **math is sound**, the assertion was too strong:
1. **IPF convergence** — `furness_intersection` converges by *matrix stability*, not target satisfaction, so `converged=True` does not imply `residual < tol`. Asserts finite/non-negative cells + finite residual instead. (Noted follow-up: audit callers that trust `converged` without checking `final_residual`.)
2. **Corridor-order** — `link_conservation` stores both directions of each EB/WB link, so the check compares unordered intersection pairs; still catches the re-sort regression that has hit this project 3×.
3. **VMT scenario linearity** — `corridor_vmt` rounds baseline and scenario VMT to 1 decimal independently, so the bound is `0.1`, not `1e-6` (single-segment generator).

### Verification
- Full forecasting suite: **94 passed, 10 skipped, 0 errors** (geo venv).
- Lean (geopandas-free) venv mirroring CI: **71 passed, 33 skipped, 0 errors**.
- Nightly profile (5000 examples × 8 properties): **8 passed, 0 counterexamples** (~3.4 min).

title: fix(balancer): stop inventing phantom movements on absent legs (int-7 EBT)
body:
## Phantom movement on absent legs (int-7 EBT bug)

A 3-leg T-intersection with **no east leg** plus a Full EB/WB corridor link drawn on that absent side caused the existing-conditions balancer to **invent a phantom eastbound-through movement** (`EBT≈415`) — flow assigned to a leg that doesn't physically exist. It was conservation-clean (delta 0), so it went **silently unflagged** on S7. Same topology class as the corridor-order bug.

**Root cause:** `balance_leg_totals` marks a leg "present" the moment a link touches it, so Stage 4c.3 reconciliation (`_adjust_leg_to_target`) couldn't tell a physical leg from a link-on-an-absent-leg, and dumped the link's canonical volume into the through-movement cell (first in the outflow set).

### Fix (3 atomic commits, each TDD + principal-engineer reviewed)

- **`e278b57` — root fix (reconciliation).** New `_raw_leg_present()` (physical presence from raw demand, link-independent). `_adjust_leg_to_target()` gates each cell on raw presence of **both** its approach and exit legs — never fills a movement on an absent leg. Structurally infeasible (no-leg) links are skipped in Stage 4c.3 so neither endpoint is perturbed, and surfaced with a dedicated **`NCHRP-LINK-NOLEG`** flag + visible delta instead of a silent phantom.
- **`ce0c720` — Level-1 forcing.** A no-leg link no longer forces leg totals at Level 1 (`balance_leg_totals` link-equality), so the **feasible endpoint's real counts are preserved** (was pulled 400→395). The link stays in the conservation table (visible delta + flag) but never forces.
- **`30e2b14` — regression guardrail.** Detection-only **`NCHRP-PHANTOM-MOVEMENT`** tripwire flags any balanced movement assigned to a raw-absent leg, so a future regression is caught loudly. Never alters volumes.

### Behavior change on S7
A Full link on an absent leg now shows a **visible structural delta + `NCHRP-LINK-NOLEG`** instead of a silent phantom. These flag the latent bad stub-leg links to remove/correct (int 7 is the first).

### Verification
- int-7 case: phantom `EBT=0`; `NCHRP-LINK-NOLEG` raised; feasible endpoint's real demand preserved; guardrail silent (fix works); delta visible.
- Valid corridors: **byte-identical** balancing output (sha256, both methods, mixed axes) — zero behavior change where legs are real; conservation deltas all 0; no new flags.
- Suites: balancer **25/0**, `run_tests.sh` **5 files / 62 checks**, forecasting **94 passed / 10 skipped**.

Follow-up (not in this PR): add the fuzz-bot invariant "no balanced movement on a `present=False` leg".

A synchronous `setState` in an effect body was an ESLint **error** (`react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`) that only surfaced when CI ran `eslint .`. ### What's added - **`scripts/verify-frontend.sh`** — the one-line gate. - Always runs `npm run lint` from `frontend/` (the exact `eslint .` CI runs); fails nonzero on any error. - `--render` also runs the headless-Chrome render check; fails nonzero if the target doesn't render. - Clears the Claude Code stdout-capture tmpfs at start (CLAUDE.md ENOSPC), best-effort/no-op elsewhere. - **`scripts/render-check.mjs`** — drives **system Chrome over the DevTools Protocol using only Node built-ins** (`child_process`, `fetch`, global `WebSocket`, `fs`). **No Playwright, no Puppeteer, no dependency.** Seeds a synthetic project into `localStorage['demandiq:project']`, navigates the route, and asserts: root element present, the anchor `` has non-zero natural dimensions (i.e. **not a blank anchor** — the exact png_base64 failure), and **zero console errors**. title: fix(backend): pin httpx==0.27.2 for anthropic 0.39.0 compat (S1 crash)
body:
## Summary

Pins a compatible `httpx` so S1 PDF extraction stops crashing at Anthropic-client construction.

`anthropic==0.39.0` constructs `httpx.Client(proxies=...)`, but `httpx` **removed the `proxies` kwarg in 0.28**. `requirements.txt` pinned `anthropic` but left `httpx` unpinned, so pip resolved `httpx 0.28.1` — and every `count_agent.extract()` call raised:

```
Client.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'proxies'
```

at `anthropic.Anthropic(...)`, before any API call. The `/extract` endpoint caught it into `errors[]` and returned **HTTP 200 with empty `results`** — so S1 failed silently-ish (a 200 that carried the error, not extracted movements).

**Fix:** pin `httpx==0.27.2` (newest `<0.28`, which still accepts `proxies=`) next to the existing `anthropic==0.39.0`. Kept `anthropic` unchanged — this is only the compatible-httpx pin, so the drift can't recur.

## Scope

**Dependency pin only — the crash fix.** One line in `backend/requirements.txt`.

This **does NOT address extraction accuracy.** A separate finding (tracked separately, not in this PR): on a real Counts Unlimited diagram-style count sheet, the vision extraction now *runs* but mis-maps movement values — it reads most numbers correctly but assigns them to the wrong movement codes (compass-orientation flips, L/T/R slot shifts, and approach-total cells leaking into movement cells), inflating intersection totals ~2.2×. That's a prompt/model issue for the vision extraction, out of scope here.

## Verification

- `anthropic.Anthropic(api_key='dummy')` constructs cleanly in `.venv-forecasting` (httpx 0.27.2, anthropic 0.39.0) — no `proxies` TypeError.
- Real `POST /extract` on a Counts Unlimited PDF → **HTTP 200, `results` non-empty, `errors: []`** (previously 200 with the error in `errors[]` and empty results).

## Not included

- No prompt changes, no `count_agent` logic changes, no accuracy work. Diff is a single line.

title: Examiner v1 — closed-loop known-answer test harness
body:
# Examiner v1 — closed-loop known-answer test harness

All-night, unattended, end-to-end testing of the real DemandIQ balance pipeline against constructed ground truth. Per seed: build a perfectly balanced corridor (answer key) → perturb every movement ±5%/±15% (min ±10 veh) → run the puzzle through the real `/balance-nchrp` endpoint exactly the way the UI does → grade against the key → document → next seed. `caffeinate -i python3.12 -m harness.loop` runs it forever; `python3.12 -m harness.run_one --seed N` reproduces any failure exactly. Runbook: `harness/README.md`.

## Endpoint + payload (confirmed from repo, per spec)

The Operator calls **`POST /balance-nchrp`** (frontend reaches it as `/api/balance-nchrp` through the Vite proxy, `vite.config.js`). `harness/operate.py::build_balance_payload` is a line-for-line port of `buildPayload` in `frontend/src/sessions/S6_RunAnalysis.jsx`: `intersections[{num,name,lat,lng}]`, `unbalanced_volumes.{AM,PM}` keyed by `str(num)` with `{value,_source}` cells stripped to bare numbers, `links[{fromNum,toNum,direction,mode}]` mapped from `fromId/toId` via the pin→num map, `link_resolution_method`, `max_iterations`, `tolerance` (same `??` fallbacks as the UI). The S8 probe calls **`POST /corridor-diagram`** and asserts real PNGs + segment labels.

## Determinism pre-check (spec precondition) — PASSED

Before any harness code: one fixed, deliberately imbalanced 4-int corridor POSTed to `/balance-nchrp` **50×** → all 50 responses byte-identical under canonical JSON (8–12 IPF iterations per intersection, so the float path was exercised). Green light per spec.

## Firewalls (structural)

- **No LLM in the numerical trust path.** Puzzler/probes/Grader/Scorekeeper are seeded, deterministic code. The only LLM call is `narrator.py`, invoked strictly post-verdict on FAIL/MARGINAL; it writes prose and may only refine an `unknown` category (a concrete deterministic category always wins; `results.csv`/ledger carry the deterministic category only). Degrades to a deterministic fallback with no API key.
- **`balancer.py` and frontend untouched.** All new code under `harness/` (+ one appended CI job). The independent math (`nchrp_math.py`) is re-derived from the NCHRP spec, never imported from the tool.
- **Operator module boundary.** `operate.py` receives only the puzzle dict; it has no import path to the Puzzler, answer key, or perturbation log.
- **Seed reproducibility.** One `random.Random(seed)` drives everything; verified: seed 4 re-run produced the identical verdict/category/signature.

## Schema gate

`harness/schema/project.schema.json` hand-derived from `projectStore.js` + `buildPayload` at SHA `96968a3`, validated by a stdlib validator (`jsonschema` isn't a repo dep). A puzzle that fails validation is a loud `input/schema` FAIL. CI runs `harness/schema/check_drift.py`, which asserts 13 exact source markers in the frontend files the schema was derived from — frontend shape drift breaks the build, not the harness's honesty.

## Probes (every cycle, all deterministic)

- **Telemetry truthfulness** — recomputes `link_conservation` (upstream/downstream/delta from balanced volumes) and `movements_review` (raw/balanced/delta) and compares to what the tool reported, exact-formula ± 1e-6. **Documented deviation:** `finalResidual` is computed inside the solver pre-rounding against Level-1 leg targets that are not in the response, so it cannot be independently recomputed without re-running the tool's own code (which would verify nothing). See `harness/knowledge/known-behaviors.md`.
- **Idempotency** — same puzzle POSTed twice must return byte-identical responses.
- **Orientation sweep** — the same abstract corridor is emitted as E–W and N–S (true 90° rotation of movements, coords, links); balanced outputs must match exactly under the mapping.
- **S8 export** — `/corridor-diagram` must return decodable PNGs for AM+PM with ≥1 segment label per period.

## Grader

Tier 1 (any red = FAIL): all `converged` true; recomputed |delta| ≤ 0.5 veh on every Full link the tool resolved; no positive movement on a leg with zero raw demand; no balanced value in (0,5). Tier 2: GEH per movement vs key — PASS ≤ 5 / MARGINAL ≤ 10 / FAIL > 10. Verdict + category + signature (sha of category+failed-checks+movement codes, int-num-agnostic so one bug = one ledger row) decided entirely in code.

## Acceptance tests — fail-then-pass (all in `harness/tests/`, CI-run, offline)

| # | Corruption | Detector fires | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Answer-key movement +300 veh | `T2-geh` FAIL, worst GEH > 10 | `test_geh_detector_fires_on_corrupted_key` |
| 2 | Positive volume on absent leg | `T1-phantom` | `test_phantom_detector_fires_on_absent_leg_volume` |
| 3 | Faked telemetry (conservation delta zeroed / review value inflated) | `probe-telemetry-truthfulness` | `test_telemetry_probe_fires_on_faked_*` (adapted per the finalResidual deviation above) |
| 4 | Backend dead (connection refused) | `pipeline-crash` recorded ×2, loop continues, ledger dedups to 1 row count 2 | `test_backend_death_records_crash_and_loop_continues` |
| 5 | Malformed puzzle (missing lat, cardinal link direction, bogus movement key) | schema gate raises with all 3 violations | `test_schema_gate_fires_on_malformed_puzzle` |
| 6 | Restore all | clean grade = PASS, no category, empty signature | `test_clean_run_is_green` |

Plus fail-then-pass tests for convergence (including an under-reported `converged` map), floor, conservation (including a response that omits `link_conservation` entries — coverage-checked against the configured links, no vacuous passes), idempotency, orientation, key-is-actually-balanced (exact link conservation across seeds/orientations/periods), generation determinism, and UI-payload parity. 17/17 green.

## Review gate

Multi-agent code review at high effort produced 16 candidate findings; verification was completed manually (the workflow's verify agents hit a session usage limit). Fixed before this PR: vacuous-pass hardening in the grader (missing `converged`/`link_conservation` entries now FAIL), secondary-probe crash isolation in the runner (a broken diagram endpoint can no longer mask accuracy grading), run-id uniquification (a same-second repro can't overwrite a forever-kept case file), persistent `checkpoints.log`, S8 payload fidelity (per-cell `b_vols`, `cols`, `title` matching `buildCorridorPayload`), derived inverse rotation, cached git SHA, cached schema load. Deliberately not changed: the 0.5-veh Tier-1 conservation threshold (spec-mandated hard invariant; the tool's own rare raw-floor 10-veh case will surface as a documented FAIL with the tool's `NCHRP-LINK-DELTA` flag in the artifacts), and per-run summary regeneration (O(n) CSV re-read is negligible at overnight scale).

## Live verification (backend on :8000, current main `96968a3`)

12-run soak after review fixes: 9 PASS · 3 FAIL — all three FAILs are **one deduped signature `adef03a02cb7`** (orientation sweep), and the soak reproduced an earlier session's results seed-for-seed. `summary.md` digest, ledger, case files (`report.md`/`evidence.md`/repro command/full JSON artifacts) all generated as specced; `run_one --seed 4` re-produced the identical verdict/category/signature.

## Findings logged along the way (diagnose-only, per firewall #2)

1. **Orientation one-quantum sensitivity (open, signature `adef03a02cb7`).** ~30% of seeds: rotating the identical corridor 90° flips a single ±5 veh quantum between two movements sharing an exit leg (e.g. EW `EBR=120/WBL=125` vs mapped NS `125/120`). GEH and conservation still pass in both orientations. Likely mechanism: IPF scaling-order float differences crossing a round-up-to-5 boundary, compensated in the paired cell by reconciliation. Documented (as an open finding, not blessed behavior) in `harness/knowledge/known-behaviors.md`.
2. **`/balance-nchrp` 500s on an empty period** (`KeyError` in `balance_leg_totals` when links exist but a period's volume dict is empty) — reachable from the UI with an AM-only project, since `buildPayload` sends `PM: {}`. The Examiner sidesteps it by generating both periods; flagged for a separate fix.

## Non-goals honored (v1)

No Mechanic (Phase 2), no headless-Chrome UI driving, no golden cases (hook folder + README ready at `harness/goldens/`), no ±30% tier, no T-intersections/missing legs, no AM+PM dual-period consistency checks, no forecasting, no Telegram.

# Examiner Telegram notifier

Adds `harness/notify.py` + `SessionNotifier`, wired into the Examiner loop. **Stacked on #15** (base `harness-examiner-v1`; GitHub will retarget to main when #15 merges — note #15 is still open, not merged as of this PR).

## ⚠️ Premise check: there is no existing fuzz-bot Telegram integration

The task said to reuse "the existing fuzz-bot Telegram integration pattern and credentials — find it in the repo — same bot, same env vars." I searched the whole repo (tracked files, env files, shell profiles): **it does not exist.** The fuzz bot (`backend/tests/forecasting/fuzz/`) is a pytest/Hypothesis suite, and its nightly workflow explicitly "does NOT open issues or modify the repo" — its only signal is the Actions tab. There are no Telegram tokens or `TELEGRAM_*`/`BOT_TOKEN` vars anywhere.

So this PR defines the contract itself, using the de-facto standard names: **`TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`** and **`TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID`** (plus `TELEGRAM_API_BASE`, overridable for tests). Standard Bot API `sendMessage` via stdlib `urllib` — no new dependencies. If the bot from another repo should be reused, it's a two-env-var setup — nothing here needs to change.

## Exactly four message types

1. **Checkpoint (every 50 runs this session):** pass rate, runs tonight, P/M/F split, failure-category counts, top signature by count. One message.
2. **New failure signature:** first occurrence **ever** — deduped in-session and seeded from `failures/index.csv` at startup, so loop restarts never re-notify a known signature. Includes the `run_one --seed N` repro command. Never per-instance.
3. **Loop death:** fires only from the loop's outer `except BaseException` — i.e. the loop itself cannot continue. Per-seed failures (including `pipeline-crash`) are absorbed upstream and never reach it.
4. **Morning summary (loop stop or 7:00 AM local, whichever first, once per session):** total runs, pass rate, trend vs previous session (persisted in gitignored `last_session.json`), and a fix-first list ranked by the Grader's severity order then count.

## Constraints honored

- **Silent no-op without env vars** — `enabled()` gates every send; all four event paths proven to emit nothing when unset.
- **Never fails the loop** — every send and every observer method is try/except-wrapped; a notify error appends to `harness_errors.log` and returns. Proven: `send()` against a dead endpoint returns `False`, logs, doesn't raise.
- **No new dependencies** — stdlib `urllib` only.
- **Reads results, never influences them** — the notifier consumes the results row after the Scorekeeper records it and reads the ledger; no imports into Grader/Puzzler/verdict code, no writes to any results file.

## Fail-then-pass evidence (all in `harness/tests/test_notify.py`, offline, CI-run)

A local HTTP capture server stands in for the Telegram API via `TELEGRAM_API_BASE`:

| Event | Red (fires) | Green (doesn't) |
|---|---|---|
| Checkpoint | fires at exactly run 50 with "50 runs tonight, 100% pass"; category × count and top-signature lines verified | silent at run 49 |
| New signature | fires with signature + repro command on first sight; fires again for a *different* signature | silent on second instance of the same signature; silent for signatures already in the ledger (restart case) |
| Loop death | `on_loop_death` fires with the traceback tail and session run count | — |
| Morning summary | `on_stop` fires with pass rate, "no previous session", ranked fix-first; next session fires with "+20.0 pts" trend; simulated 7 AM boundary fires mid-loop | second summary never sent after the 7 AM one (once per session) |
| No env vars | — | all four events emit nothing; full `loop.main()` with env unset **and** a dead backend exits 0 with both seeds recorded `pipeline-crash` |

Suite total: 27 passed (17 existing detector tests + 10 notifier tests). Live check: 3-seed loop against the real backend with the notifier wired and env unset — 3 PASS, no behavioral change.

title: fix(balancer): rotation-invariant tie-break in leg reconciliation
body:
## Problem

The Examiner orientation sweep found the balancer is not orientation-invariant (signature `adef03a02cb7`, 1,060 recorded hits): the same corridor run N–S vs E–W flips a single ±5 rounding quantum between two movements sharing an exit leg. Seed 4: AM int 1 NBR/SBL swap 120/125. Case file: `harness/failures/20260711-141443-seed4/`.

## Diagnosis

The proposed hypothesis — float accumulation order in IPF/normalization — was **falsified** by instrumentation: Level-1 leg targets and pre-round IPF matrices are **bit-identical** (max diff exactly 0.0) across orientations.

The actual root cause is in Stage 4c.3 post-round reconciliation. `_adjust_leg_to_target`'s decrement branch sorted candidate cells by `(value, movement-code string)`, breaking value ties by the compass-labeled string. Those labels relabel under 90° rotation, so the same physical tie picks different physical cells per orientation:

| frame | tied cells (same physical pair) | string tie-break picks |
|---|---|---|
| EW | SBL / NBR at 125 | `'S' > 'N'` → SBL |
| NS | EBL / WBR at 125 | `'W' > 'E'` → WBR (the *other* physical cell) |

Ties can only diverge on **outflow** legs (three different compass prefixes per tier, e.g. `EBT/SBL/NBR`) — hence the "two movements sharing an exit leg" symptom. Approach tiers share one prefix, so their string order happens to survive rotation.

## Fix (one change, `backend/balancer.py` only)

Break decrement value-ties by **tier position** — the leg-relative L/T/R spec order, which maps 1:1 under rotation — mirroring the increment branch's existing `max()` semantics. No NCHRP methodology change: 0.01 tolerance, 5-veh round-up floor, Larger/Average resolution, and normalization logic are untouched.

## Proof (fail-then-pass)

- **Before:** `run_one --seed 4` → `FAIL category=unknown` on probe-orientation-sweep, signature `adef03a02cb7` (reproduced at 17:50 on `f615f55`, matching 5 prior recorded runs).
- **After:** seeds **4, 5, 9** → PASS, with worst GEH unchanged per seed (1.826 / 2.236 / 3.947) — accuracy untouched, only the orientation probe flipped.
- **100-seed batch:** signature `adef03a02cb7` occurs **zero** times (96 PASS; 1 MARGINAL = seed 94's pre-existing `f1bf8e87b69d` accuracy-drift, identical verdict/GEH before and after).
- **No regression:** seeds 1, 2, 3, 10, 11, 12 PASS with verdicts, worst GEH, and worst movement identical to every pre-fix run.
- **Determinism:** 50 identical POSTs → byte-identical bodies. Backend suite: `ALL SUITES PASSED (5 files)`; harness detector suite: 27 passed.

`harness/knowledge/lessons.md` gains its first real entry (symptom → cause → fix → proof seeds). `harness/failures/index.csv` (gitignored run-state) updated locally: `adef03a02cb7` → `fixed,fdcd29e` after the proof.

title: Examiner v2: difficulty tiers — long corridors + T-intersections
body:
## What

Examiner v1's config (3–6 four-leg intersections) saturated at ~100% post-fix pass rate over ~22k seeds — it becomes **Tier A**, byte-identical per seed, and three escalation tiers join it:

| Tier | Intersections | Legs |
|---|---|---|
| A (default) | 3–6 | all 4-leg — pre-tier behavior, unchanged |
| B | 5–20 | all 4-leg (error propagation down long chains) |
| C | 3–6 | seeded ~50/50 four-leg / 3-leg (T) |
| D | 5–20 | mixed per Tier C |

Generation is a pure function of **(seed, tier)**. Tier A keeps the exact pre-tier RNG stream; B/C/D run on their own string-seeded stream (sha512-stable) and can never perturb it. `run_one --seed N` with no tier arg reproduces exactly what it did before; `--tier B|C|D` selects the new tiers. The loop rotates tiers per run (seeded per seed; default mix A 20 / B 30 / C 30 / D 20, `--tier-mix` configurable, `--tier` pins one for soaks).

**T-intersections** follow the real frontend representation, derived from source (`S3_ApproachConfig.jsx toggleDne`, `projectStore.setCellValue`): the absent approach key stays present as `{exists: false, lanes: [], stopControlled: false}`, and the absent leg's movement keys are **omitted** from `volumes` — never nulled or zeroed. The absent leg is always one of the two cross-street legs, so the corridor chain stays connected. The answer key omits the same movements and routes each corridor constraint's remainder to its surviving member, keeping link conservation exact by construction. title: feat(backend): RECON-ADJUST — disclose large reconciliation adjustments (Fix 1)
body:
## What

**Disclosure only — not an accuracy fix.** The Examiner diagnosis (`harness/knowledge/diagnosis-through-inflation.md`, checked in here) proved one mechanism behind all four open accuracy-drift signatures: post-round reconciliation concentrates accumulated adjacent-link disagreement onto the corridor **through** movement — the only cell shared by both adjacent link constraints; a T-intersection halves the absorbing corners — inflating a low-volume through up to 4× raw (seed 34093 PM int 7: WBT raw 50 → balanced 210) while post-round link conservation closes exactly 0.0. **Zero existing QC surfaces can see it.**

New `reconciliation_adjustment_flags()` in `backend/balancer.py`, wired in `app.py` beside `source_outlier_flags`: after balancing, each movement's balanced value is compared to its raw input and a `RECON-ADJUST` qc_flag is emitted when **both** |balanced − raw| ≥ 30 veh **and** GEH(balanced, raw) ≥ 5. Covers both directions (inflation *and* reduction — complements, does not replace, the known drop-below-raw NCHRP behavior). Example message:

> Int 7 WBT (PM): raw 50 → balanced 210 (+320%, GEH 14.0). Large reconciliation adjustment (inflation) — the balanced value is driven by adjacent link targets, not the source count. Engineer review recommended.

One deliberate deviation from the prompt's example: the message reports **GEH(balanced, raw) = 14.0** — the tool-computable number — not the case file's 12.9, which is GEH vs the *answer key* the tool cannot know.

No balancing math, targets, resolution, rounding, tolerance, or convergence logic touched.

title: The Forger: known-answer test harness for S1 PDF extraction (draft: live gate pending API credits)
body:
## ⚠️ Draft — one live acceptance gate outstanding (API credits)

Everything deterministic is built, tested fail-then-pass, and green. The single remaining non-negotiable — **the known bug must reproduce on Style D against the real extractor** — requires live API calls, and the account currently has **no credit balance** (real billing-400 on a valid key, probed 2026-07-18; request IDs in `harness/forger/runs/20260718-1545*`). Once credits are added, the gate is:

```bash
python3.12 -m harness.forger.batch --n 20 --style D          # bug must express as MAP-ERR
python3.12 -m harness.forger.batch --n 1 --style D --repeat 5  # live variance measurement
```

If 20 Style D sheets extract perfectly, the renderer isn't faithful — the layout gets iterated until the bug expresses, and the triggering feature documented. The two probe runs incidentally **live-proved the CRASH path**: both recorded `CRASH` verdicts with signatures and the session continued.

## What this is

The Forger: a known-answer test harness for S1 PDF extraction (`count_agent.py` via Claude vision), closing the no-labeled-PDFs gap. Examiner philosophy throughout — known answer first, deterministic grading, signature dedup, case files, fail-then-pass detectors. New code under `harness/forger/` only; `count_agent.py`, the Examiner, and `balancer.py` untouched.

**The firewall stands even though the system under test is an LLM:** no LLM generates the answer key, renders the PDF, or decides pass/fail. Extractor variance is recorded per-run and never averaged; batches are hard-capped at 200 runs with per-run token logging — no unbounded loops.

- **Forger** (`sheets.py`): per (seed, style), 12 movements 5–1500 + derivable approach/grand totals, rendered via reportlab (invariant mode → **PDF bytes deterministic per (seed, style)**). Style T = NDS/Quality Counts tabular (15-min bins summing exactly to peak-hour). Style D = Counts Unlimited-like diagram (plan view, per-approach trios at arrow positions with drawn turn arrows, boxed approach totals, grand total, compass, N-up/E-up rotation). All 17 numbers per period pairwise >10 apart so exact-value grading is unambiguous.
- **Operator** (`operate.py`): calls `count_agent.extract(path, api_key)` — the exact function `/extract` uses, no vendor_hint, same as the webapp. Raw model output + token usage captured via a read-only recording proxy around the Anthropic client (runtime observation; no source change). Never raises — CRASH is a verdict.
- **Grader** (`grader.py`): per-movement `CORRECT` / `DIGIT-ERR` / `MAP-ERR` (sub-patterns `NS-FLIP`, `EW-FLIP`, `LTR-SHIFT`, `OTHER-SWAP`) / `TOTAL-AS-MOVEMENT` / `OMISSION` / `HALLUCINATION`; sheet-level total ratio (the 2.2× symptom); verdicts `PASS`/`DIGIT-ONLY`/`MAP-FAIL`/`MIXED`/`CRASH`; signatures hash (style, classes, sub-patterns) — never seed values.
- **Scorekeeper**: `results.csv` (one row per run, repeats included), case files with `--seed N --style D` repro commands, signature ledger, `summary.md` with verdict rates by style, error-class histogram, MAP sub-pattern tracker, repeat-seed variance table, token spend.

## Acceptance status

| # | Gate | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Known bug reproduces on Style D | **BLOCKED — API credits** (command above) |
| 2 | Corrupted answer-key value → Grader flags it | ✅ offline test |
| 3 | Hand-built N/S flip → MAP-ERR / NS-FLIP | ✅ offline test |
| 4 | Total-in-movement-slot → TOTAL-AS-MOVEMENT | ✅ offline test |
| 5 | Killed API key → CRASH recorded, batch continues | ✅ offline test **+ live billing-400 proof** |
| 6 | Seed repeated 5× → variance per-run, never averaged | ✅ offline test (live rerun with credits) |

17 offline tests, written first and watched fail. Full suite: `python3.12 -m pytest harness/forger/tests -q` — no API, no cost.

## Notes for review

- **Style D provenance:** the repo holds no Counts Unlimited layout notes and no sample PDFs (searched exhaustively incl. git history — the prior analysis was never committed). The layout derives from industry-standard TMC diagram conventions + the bug's recorded symptoms (N/S flips, L/T/R shifts, totals-as-movements). Documented in `sheets.py` and the README.
- **Corpus firewall:** every PDF carries `forger-synthetic=true` metadata; the never-train-on-the-exam rule is documented in `harness/knowledge/known-behaviors.md`.
- **New dep:** `reportlab` (harness-side only; `backend/requirements.txt` untouched).

body:
**Fix: the corridor through no longer swallows link disagreements at T-intersections.** Written by Hermes. Do not merge until the owner answers the two OPEN items in `Docs/through-inflation-fix.md`.

## What was wrong
Seed 34093, PM, intersection 7 (a T): westbound through, true 60, count 50, **balanced 210**. The neighbouring links disagreed by about 240 and 170 cars. Because the cross-street total was held at its own count, the through was the only number at that T free to absorb the change, so it took all of it. Link totals still closed exactly, so nothing flagged it except RECON-ADJUST.

## The fix
`backend/balancer.py`, `balance_nchrp` second pass: a leg is held to its target only if it is on a balanced link (Full / Land Use). A side-street leg with no link to a neighbour now floats, so a link change is shared by every movement on that link, by volume. Same case after: **85** instead of 210. Links still close.

## Proof
Direct balancer runs, 500 corridors per tier (both peaks). Count of corridors whose worst movement is past GEH 5 against the true volume (GEH 5 is the usual count-acceptance line):
- Tier A: 2 → 0
- Tier B: 13 → 2
- Tier C: 39 → 1
- Tier D: 92 → 0
- Worse: 1 of 2,000 (tier C seed 104, a northbound right, true 145: 210 → 220).

The 4 failing Examiner cases are frozen in `backend/tests/through_inflation_cases.json` (test written first and committed red: 8e8ac77).

title: Fix: 'Start a new project?' dialog hidden under the map
body:
Written by Hermes. Sweep 2026-11-15, item 3 (risk: data loss).

## Problem
On any screen with a map (Map, Review movements, Results, Network Match), **New project** dims the page but the map stays on top of the "Start a new project?" dialog. You can't see the dialog, but its **Delete & start new** button (deletes the project, no undo) still takes clicks.

Cause: `TopBar.jsx` renders the dialog inside `.di-top`, and `shell.css` gives `.di-top` `position: relative; z-index: 5`. That caps the dialog's `z-index: 2000` at 5, under Leaflet's panes (400).

## Fix
`NewProjectDialog` renders through `createPortal(…, document.body)`. One file, both callers (TopBar and S8) covered.

## Test (fails before, passes after)
New `--on-top <selector>` option in `scripts/render-check.mjs`: after the `--click`, it finds the lowest z-index set on the element or any positioned ancestor and fails if it is 1000 or less (Leaflet panes are 400, controls up to 1000). Added the invocation to CLAUDE.md.

```
node scripts/render-check.mjs --route /results --root .di-s7 --image .di-s7-card__img \
  --click "New project" --on-top .di-modal-backdrop
```
- Before: `FAIL — .di-modal-backdrop is capped at z-index 5 by "di-top", so the map (...) paints over it` (same on `/review-movements`)
- After: `PASS — /results rendered; .di-s7-card__img = 600x600; 0 console errors` (and `/review-movements` passes)

Screenshots (1400×1600, Results): before, the right half of the dialog, including **Delete & start new**, is cut off by the map. After, the whole dialog shows above the blurred map.

## Gates
- `scripts/verify-frontend.sh`: lint PASS
- `--render`: run as `node scripts/render-check.mjs …` directly, because under git-bash on Windows `verify-frontend.sh --render` passes a `/c/...` path to native node and can't find the script (a gate-script problem, already known, not part of this fix).

`MovementPickerModal` (S3), the S2 renumber dialog and the S4 bulk-paste dialog render inside the page with no z-index on any ancestor, and S3 has no map. They are not capped.

title: Decision: MTC snap distance (Regents Blvd is 156 ft from the model road)
body:
Written by Hermes, from sweep 2026-11-15 item 5.

**Question for the owner:** should the forecasting snap distance stay at 150 ft, or go up for MTC (Bay Area)?

PR (mid-link snapping) lets an intersection snap onto an MTC link line when no model node is close by. On the real MTC 2015 file:

| Place | Distance to the MTC road | Result with 150 ft |
|---|---|---|
| Union City Blvd & Jean Dr | 34 ft | matched |
| Union City Blvd & Dyer St | 30 ft | matched |
| Oakwood Dr & El Camino Real | 60 ft | bound for review (El Camino runs diagonally) |
| **Union City Blvd & Regents Blvd** | **156 ft** | **not matched**, engineer types the legs in |

MTC draws one line down the middle of a wide arterial, so a pin at the curb can be more than 150 ft from it.

Options:
1. **Keep 150 ft.** Regents-type cases use "Enter manually". This is the safest choice ("favour false negatives").
2. **200 ft for MTC only.** Regents matches. There's a small risk of binding to a parallel road.
3. **Keep 150 ft, and change the message.** Today it says "nearest model node is 2054 ft away". It could say the road is 156 ft away, so the engineer can move the pin.

Code: `backend/forecasting/matcher.py:32` (`SNAP_TOLERANCE_FT`). The split uses the same value in `adapters/mtc.py`.

title: Fix: MTC matching snaps onto the link line, not only its ends
body:
Written by Hermes. Sweep 2026-11-15, item 5.

## Problem
Bay Area (MTC) forecasting couldn't match intersections that fall between model nodes, and MTC links can be about a mile long.
- `adapters/mtc.py` kept a link only when one of its **ends** was within 300 ft.
- The matcher snaps to **nodes** within 150 ft.
- So Union City got 12 unmatched legs, and Oakwood/El Camino Real failed with "no MTC road within 300 ft … is the project inside the nine Bay Area counties?"

## Fix (MTC adapter only; matcher, refinement and SANDAG unchanged)
1. Keep a link when its **line** passes within the ingest radius, not only its ends.
2. If no model node is within the matcher's snap distance (still 150 ft, `SNAP_TOLERANCE_FT`), split the nearest link at the intersection when it is that close:
   - The two halves (`<lo>-<hi>a`, `<lo>-<hi>b`) meet at a new node `-(i+1)`.
   - Both halves keep the link's AB/BA flows. The length is split in proportion, so VMT is unchanged.
   - Base and horizon get the same split because both use the same project points. That keeps refinement's link_id pairing and `inbound_to(node)` working untouched.

## Test (fails before, passes after)
`tests/forecasting/test_mtc_adapter.py::test_intersection_mid_link_snaps_onto_the_link`: a synthetic 1,200 m two-way link, with the intersection 33 ft off its middle.
- Before: `ValueError: ingest_mtc: no MTC road within 300 ft of the project intersections …`
- After: NB/SB matched with the right inbound volumes (500/700), the halves' lengths add up to the link, and the base and horizon link_ids are the same.
- `pytest tests/forecasting`: 193 passed, 10 skipped (skips need real data or keys, same as main).

## Repro on the real MTC 2015/2050 files (sweep points, read-only)
| Place | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Union City Blvd & Jean Dr | node 1,145 ft away, unmatched | snapped 34 ft onto Union City Blvd, NB/SB matched |
| Union City Blvd & Dyer St | node 189 ft away, unmatched | snapped 30 ft, NB/SB matched |
| Oakwood Dr & El Camino Real | ingest failed | snapped 60 ft. El Camino's two halves are bound **for review** (ambiguous), because it runs diagonally, more than 35° off E/W. That is the existing safety rule. |
| Union City Blvd & Regents Blvd | unmatched | still unmatched: the road is **156 ft** away, just past 150 ft. See decision issue #39. |

Cross streets that aren't in the model (Jean, Dyer, Oakwood) stay unmatched, as before. The engineer enters them by hand.

## Left
- #39 (decision-needed): the snap distance for MTC (the Regents case), and the wording of the "off-model" message.
- Network Match shows "snapped to node -2" for a split point. That is cosmetic, and the wording isn't changed here.
- Other adapters (SANDAG, upload) still filter by link ends. SANDAG has a node at nearly every cross street, so it works today.
